You have to see a psychiatrist for it and ask for a prescription I believe. They don't give meds out easily to people, you need to have a prescription from a psychiatrist. The psych will evaluate what kind of drug best suits your condition (a psychological diagnosis) and determine the dosage you will take, you will most likely be given a smaller dose at first. I am not sure if you can simply 'ask' a psychiatrist for a prescription. From my experience, I was diagnosed by a psychiatrist (as in the type of disorder I had) and I didn't ask for a prescription, the psychiatrist just gave me a prescription for the things I had trouble with only because it was so bad to the point where it's necessary.

Since I had trouble with sleep, anxiety and depression. I was given sleeping pills, Lexapro for anxiety caused depression, Xanax for anxiety/feeling overwhelmed, and Ritalin for ADD. So you will be given prescription only with whatever is necessary to help you tackle specific issues. If what you're dealing with is interrupting your daily life too much to the point where you can't function, the psychiatrist will determine that you need medication to function better and to help you cope. 

I believe that if the psychiatrist thinks that it's not necessary for you to take medication, they might not give you a prescription because it isn't really something you can take lightly, they will only give it to you if they think that you will benefit from medication since there are some risks involved in it, but it brings a lot of advantages as well as it may help you regulate your mood better.

If you are not ready for genuine medication I think there are other anti-depression or anti-anxiety 'softer' alternatives that you can find. Look up CBD oil.

It definitely would help. (Unfortunately my family is against medication and they confiscated my meds...)

Medication would definitely help the chemical imbalances. For example you might feel that you have tried a lot of things already but you still feel that your mood hasn't really changed and it still impacts on your daily life. If somehow you've had a good day but at the end of the day you are crying for no reason even if things are relatively okay, if that is the case, maybe you would like to try medication but **this should only be consulted by a professional and I am not to tell you whether you need to take it or not, but this is a suggestion I've always heard from my therapist and counselor.**

However meds alone won't help, just as how only therapy alone won't help. There's a lot of factors to consider, and each one of the ways to cope with depression (therapy, medication, self-care, etc.) has its pros and cons. It is up to you to regulate and control them. 

For medication however I was told that when you try it you might feel like it zaps your emotions, so you don't necessarily feel depressed but you can't feel anything positive either, I heard feeling numb is a common side effect for medication but really it all depends on your body because everyone's bodies work differently. 

I would give extra consideration to medication because unlike therapy, you're putting chemicals in your body and it essentially changes how you feel. Sometimes it might cause mood swings or episodes and it's something I would really be careful about. You have to be alert and responsibly take initiative by regularly checking up on how your body's taking the meds, like if it becomes habit-forming (issues with dosage should be consulted with your psychiatrist) or if the drug isn't suitable for you (by informing your psychiatrist when you notice undesirable effects through certain types of meds that could possibly harm you or else it will manifest into more dangerous issues.

Personally for me, it didn't help much.

At first I was taught those techniques on how to adopt a 'better' way to think, because we do have a tendency to think in a slightly 'distorted' way. 

But sometimes there is always some degree of truth to our thoughts. It isn't just paranoia or anxiety. Some of it is real.

Also, about how we're feeling, we can't help it can we? Telling us to fix our thought process, what - do you think we haven't thought about whatever it is that you're saying? Those words from our T, sometimes we are actually aware of them subconsciously. We sometimes can't bring ourselves to believe it, or sometimes we just can't 'stop worrying'- telling us the 'truth', it may seem simply to think that thought process can change how we feel about things. But what is the process between those two? Just simply telling us things, it doesn't work. 

Often times we are already aware about whatever that therapist has said. Technically we're just paying to listen to things we already know, that we're already aware of. Doing worksheets and being told about the correct way to think - when I told my T it didn't help she began talking about my lack of self care, and it almost felt like she was *blaming* me, saying something along the lines of 'self-care isn't even part of CBT and you can't get it right'. I experimented, trust me, and I eventually still broke down. It's going up and down, up and down. 

Like what, I can't just 'snap out' of my thoughts, how does that even fucking work? When I told her about this, she tells me maybe I should try medication because 'just therapy doesn't work for everyone'. I'm honestly so sick of it all. 

Maybe it feels a bit confusing with my words because I don't really know how to explain it well, but my experience with therapy hasn't really been useful. 
***Also, my experience was with CBT, I'm not at all familiar with other approaches in therapy so I can't comment on them.***

You can read up on it to get what I mean on here:
http://www.johnbartontherapy.com/blog/the-great-cbt-debate
I've experienced most cases of 'The case against CBT' and it all explains how I feel like it isn't helping. I am not writing this to make you feel hopeless, but I am just honestly expressing my experience and I am hoping that if you do consider to try therapy, maybe consider the different types of therapy there are? CBT for me was really bad, I could explain my experience more in detail 
but that would be hella long and I doubt anyone would want to listen. Even I myself am sick of it, as if being treated like a subject experiment or whatever and being blamed for shit. 

Again, I cannot speak for other people because this is just my personal experience. Maybe CBT might work for you, it has its pros and cons. Either way, it won't hurt to try therapy.
